native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is about 28 pages (n=18, SD≈7.4, median 27.5, range 16–45), whereas in Psychology it is about 11 pages (n=90, SD≈6.2, median 9.0, range 1–31). Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project are therefore roughly 2.5 times (28/11 ≈ 2.55) longer than those in the Psychology replication project.
native_result.WorkflowB: Data source: meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows; the only file containing 'length' = pages of original paper; project mapping ee=Experimental Economics, rpp=Psychology per schema, cross-validated against the second dataset which has 18 'Experimental Economics' rows and no length column). Filters: project in {ee, rpp}; drop==False (7 rpp rows flagged for data quality, e.g. rpp.46 with n.o=230025). Computed mean/SD/median/min/max of 'length' per project: EE n=18 mean=28.00 (SD 7.37, median 27.5); Psychology n=90 mean=11.00 (SD 6.16, median 9.0); ratio 2.545. Sensitivity: dropping the exact duplicate record rpp.149 gives 11.045 (n=89); unique original papers by title gives 11.011 (n=88); keeping drop==True rows gives 11.217 (n=97) — all within 11.0–11.2, so the conclusion is robust. No missing or zero length values; no aggregated rows in ee/rpp (aggregated is NaN there).

sub_hypo.text: Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project average 28 pages, compared with 11 pages in the Psychology replication project, making them approximately 2.55 times longer.
sub_hypo.context: Original papers in meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv restricted to project ee (Experimental Economics) and rpp (Psychology), with drop==False; seven Psychology rows flagged for data quality are excluded.
sub_hypo.relations: Experimental Economics: n=18, mean length=28.00 pages, SD=7.37, median=27.5, range=16–45. Psychology: n=90, mean length=11.00 pages, SD=6.16, median=9.0, range=1–31. The ratio of mean lengths is 2.545 (approximately 2.55). Sensitivity analyses yield Psychology means of 11.045 after removing exact duplicate rpp.149 (n=89), 11.011 for unique original papers by title (n=88), and 11.217 when including drop==True rows (n=97), preserving the approximately 2.5-fold difference.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is about 28 pages (n=18, SD≈7.4, median 27.5, range 16–45), whereas in Psychology it is about 11 pages (n=90, SD≈6.2, median 9.0, range 1–31). Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project are therefore roughly 2.5 times (28/11 ≈ 2.55) longer than those in the Psychology replication project.
